Callback function that is fired when the slider's value changed.
You can pull out the new value by accessing `event.target.value` (any).

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the change:

- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'none'` when the change is triggered without a specific interaction
props.onValueCommitted:
Callback function that is fired when the `pointerup` is triggered.
**Warning**: This is a generic event not a change event.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the commit:

- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'none'` when the commit occurs without a specific interaction
props.step:
The granularity with which the slider can step through values. (A "discrete" slider.)
The `min` prop serves as the origin for the valid values.
We recommend (max - min) to be evenly divisible by the step.
props.thumbAlignment:
How the thumb(s) are aligned relative to `Slider.Control` when the value is at `min` or `max`:
- `center`: The center of the thumb is aligned with the control edge
- `edge`: The thumb is inset within the control such that its edge is aligned with the control edge
- `edge-client-only`: Same as `edge` but renders after React hydration on the client, reducing bundle size in return
props.thumbCollisionBehavior:
Controls how thumbs behave when they collide during pointer interactions.

- `'push'` (default): Thumbs push each other without restoring their previous positions when dragged back.
- `'swap'`: Thumbs swap places when dragged past each other.
- `'none'`: Thumbs cannot move past each other; excess movement is ignored.

AutocompleteElement.mode:
Controls how the autocomplete behaves with respect to list filtering and inline autocompletion.
- `list` (default): items are dynamically filtered based on the input value. The input value does not change
  based on the active item.
- `both`: items are dynamically filtered based on the input value, which will temporarily change based on the
  active item (inline autocompletion).
- `inline`: items are static (not filtered), and the input value will temporarily change based on the active item
  (inline autocompletion).
- `none`: items are static (not filtered), and the input value will not change based on the active item.

SelectItemElement.label:
Specifies the text label to use when the item is matched during keyboard text navigation.

Defaults to the item text content if not provided.
SelectItemElement.value: A unique value that identifies this select item.

SelectItemIndicatorElement.keep-mounted: Whether to keep the HTML element in the DOM when the item is not selected.

SelectPositionerElement.align: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.
SelectPositionerElement.align-item-with-trigger:
Whether the positioner overlaps the trigger so the selected item's text is aligned with the trigger's value text.
This only applies to mouse input and is automatically disabled if there is not enough space.
SelectPositionerElement.align-offset: Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
SelectPositionerElement.arrow-padding:
Minimum distance to maintain between the arrow and the edges of the popup.

Use it to prevent the arrow element from hanging out of the rounded corners of a popup.
SelectPositionerElement.collision-padding: Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary.
SelectPositionerElement.disable-anchor-tracking: Whether to disable the popup from tracking any layout shift of its positioning anchor.
SelectPositionerElement.position-method: Determines which CSS `position` property to use.
SelectPositionerElement.side:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.
SelectPositionerElement.side-offset: Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
SelectPositionerElement.sticky:
Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after
the anchor element was scrolled out of view.

SelectScrollArrowPart.keep-mounted: Whether to keep the arrow in the DOM while the list cannot be scrolled in its direction.

SelectTriggerElement.disabled: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

SelectValueElement.placeholder:
The placeholder value to display when no value is selected.
This is overridden by `children` if specified, or by a null item's label in `items`.

SliderElement.default-value:
The uncontrolled value of the slider when it’s initially rendered.

To render a controlled slider, use the `value` attribute instead.
SliderElement.disabled: Whether the slider should ignore user interaction.
SliderElement.large-step: The granularity with which the slider can step through values when using Page Up/Page Down or Shift + Arrow Up/Arrow Down.
SliderElement.locale:
The locale used by `Intl.NumberFormat` when formatting the value.
Defaults to the user's runtime locale.
SliderElement.max:
The maximum allowed value of the slider.
Should not be equal to min.
SliderElement.min:
The minimum allowed value of the slider.
Should not be equal to max.
SliderElement.min-steps-between-values: The minimum steps between values in a range slider.
SliderElement.name: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.
SliderElement.step:
The granularity with which the slider can step through values. (A "discrete" slider.)
The `min` attribute serves as the origin for the valid values.
We recommend (max - min) to be evenly divisible by the step.
SliderElement.thumb-alignment:
How the thumb(s) are aligned relative to `<prefix>-slider-control` when the value is at `min` or `max`:
- `center`: The center of the thumb is aligned with the control edge
- `edge`: The thumb is inset within the control such that its edge is aligned with the control edge
SliderElement.thumb-collision-behavior:
Controls how thumbs behave when they collide during pointer interactions.

- `'push'` (default): Thumbs push each other without restoring their previous positions when dragged back.
- `'swap'`: Thumbs swap places when dragged past each other.
- `'none'`: Thumbs cannot move past each other; excess movement is ignored.

SliderThumbElement.disabled: Whether the thumb should ignore user interaction.
SliderThumbElement.index:
The index of the thumb in a range slider: the index of its value in the slider's `value`. Without it, the
position of the thumb among the thumbs.
SliderThumbElement.label: The accessible name of the thumb.

SnippetCopyButtonElement.disabled: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.
SnippetCopyButtonElement.reset-delay: Time in milliseconds before resetting the copy status to idle.

SnippetElement.disable-copy: Whether to disable the copy functionality.
SnippetElement.symbol: The symbol to display in the snippet.

SnippetLineElement.value: The text copied for this line. Defaults to the line's text content without its symbols.

SwitchElement.checked:
Whether the switch is currently active.

To render an uncontrolled switch, use the `default-checked` attribute instead.
SwitchElement.default-checked:
Whether the switch is initially active.

To render a controlled switch, use the `checked` attribute instead.
SwitchElement.disabled: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.
SwitchElement.name: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.
SwitchElement.read-only: Whether the user should be unable to activate or deactivate the switch.
SwitchElement.required: Whether the user must activate the switch before submitting a form.

TabsElement.default-value:
The default value. Use when the component is not controlled.
When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active.
TabsElement.value:
The value of the currently active `Tab`. Use when the component is controlled.
When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active.

TabsListElement.activate-on-focus:
Whether to automatically change the active tab on arrow key focus.
Otherwise, tabs will be activated using <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> key press.
TabsListElement.loop-focus:
Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first item
when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys.

TabsPanelElement.value:
The value of the panel: it is shown while the tab with the same value is selected. Without it, the index of the
panel.

TabsTabElement.disabled: Whether the tab ignores user interaction.
TabsTabElement.value:
The value of the Tab.
When not specified, the value is the child position index.

ToastActionElement.disabled: Whether the button ignores user interaction.

ToastCloseElement.disabled: Whether the button ignores user interaction.

ToastElement.swipe-direction: Direction(s) in which the toast can be swiped to dismiss.

ToastProviderElement.limit:
The maximum number of toasts that can be displayed at once.
When the limit is reached, the oldest toast will be removed to make room for the new one.
ToastProviderElement.timeout:
The default amount of time (in ms) before a toast is auto dismissed.
A value of `0` will prevent the toast from being dismissed automatically.

ToggleElement.default-pressed:
Whether the toggle button is currently pressed.
This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `pressed`.
ToggleElement.disabled: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.
ToggleElement.pressed:
Whether the toggle button is currently pressed.
This is the controlled counterpart of `default-pressed`.
ToggleElement.value:
A unique string that identifies the toggle when used
inside a toggle group.

ToggleGroupElement.default-value:
The open state of the toggle group represented by an array of
the values of all pressed toggle buttons.
This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `value`.
ToggleGroupElement.disabled: Whether the toggle group should ignore user interaction.
ToggleGroupElement.loop-focus:
Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first item
when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys.
ToggleGroupElement.multiple:
When `false` only one item in the group can be pressed. If any item in
the group becomes pressed, the others will become unpressed.
When `true` multiple items can be pressed.
ToggleGroupElement.orientation: The visual orientation of the group: which arrow keys move the focus.

ToolbarElement.cols:
The number of columns. When greater than 1, the toolbar is arranged into
a grid.
ToolbarElement.disabled: Whether every item of the toolbar ignores user interaction.
ToolbarElement.loop-focus: If `true`, using keyboard navigation will wrap focus to the other end of the toolbar once the end is reached.

ToolbarGroupElement.disabled: When `true` all toolbar items in the group are disabled.

ToolbarItemPart.disabled: Whether the item ignores user interaction.
ToolbarItemPart.focusable-when-disabled: Whether the item stays focusable while disabled, so the arrow keys still reach it.

TooltipElement.default-open:
Whether the tooltip is initially open.

To render a controlled tooltip, use the `open` attribute instead.
TooltipElement.disable-hoverable-popup: Whether the tooltip contents can be hovered without closing the tooltip.
TooltipElement.open: Whether the tooltip is currently open.
TooltipElement.track-cursor-axis: Determines which axis the tooltip should track the cursor on.

TooltipPositionerElement.align: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.
TooltipPositionerElement.align-offset: Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
TooltipPositionerElement.arrow-padding:
Minimum distance to maintain between the arrow and the edges of the popup.

Use it to prevent the arrow element from hanging out of the rounded corners of a popup.
TooltipPositionerElement.collision-padding: Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary.
TooltipPositionerElement.disable-anchor-tracking: Whether to disable the popup from tracking any layout shift of its positioning anchor.
TooltipPositionerElement.keep-mounted: Whether to keep the popup in the DOM while the tooltip is closed.
TooltipPositionerElement.position-method: Determines which CSS `position` property to use.
TooltipPositionerElement.side:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.
TooltipPositionerElement.side-offset: Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
TooltipPositionerElement.sticky:
Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after
the anchor element was scrolled out of view.

TooltipProviderElement.close-delay: How long to wait before closing a tooltip. Specified in milliseconds.
TooltipProviderElement.delay: How long to wait before opening a tooltip. Specified in milliseconds.
TooltipProviderElement.timeout:
Another tooltip will open instantly if the previous tooltip
is closed within this timeout. Specified in milliseconds.

TooltipTriggerElement.close-delay: How long to wait before closing the tooltip. Specified in milliseconds.
TooltipTriggerElement.delay: How long to wait before opening the tooltip. Specified in milliseconds.
TooltipTriggerElement.disabled: Whether the trigger does not open the tooltip.
TooltipTriggerElement.primary:
Marks this trigger as the primary trigger for positioning.
Used when the tooltip is opened via TooltipMultiple sync.
If multiple triggers are marked as primary, the first one wins.
